title: I Got Paid to Watch TV (2026 Mediaprobe Review)
promo_conflict: The host says the application link is in the description; any affiliate or sponsorship relationship is not stated.

stated_problem.quote: Number one, would they really pay? And number two, is it worth your time?
stated_problem.speaker: Side Hustle Nation host (unnamed)

idea.name: Paid TV audience-research panel
idea.one_liner: Viewers apply to watch assigned shows with a sensor and share reactions; research companies and networks pay for the audience data, with participants receiving part of the income.
idea.customer: MediaProbe/M Panel participants earn from sessions; research companies and TV networks buy the audience reaction data.
idea.offer: Watch assigned content while using a sensor and app, then answer questions about the show and ads.
idea.revenue_model: Research clients pay MediaProbe for audience data; MediaProbe shares part of that income with participants, who are paid in gift cards.

key_quotes.quote: And then companies and TV networks pay media probe for this data to see how audiences actually feel about their content. And then they, in theory, pass along the portion of that income to viewers like you and me.
Generally, media probe offers about $5 per hour of watch time, sometimes a little bit higher, which isn't a bad gig.
In total, I made 10 bucks from MrBeast and 30 bucks from watching a couple World Cup games.

claims.claim: The host guesses that sending sensors to participants has a real cost.
claims.quote: My guess is that's because there's a real cost to do the company sending out these sensors.

claims.claim: The host had to take an approximately five-minute screening call.
claims.quote: In my case, I even had to get on like a five minute call with their team to verify I was game to test this out.

claims.claim: The host received about five to ten session invitations per month.
claims.quote: It has to be one of their assigned shows, which I've been getting like five to 10 invites a month, but it still took a while to connect with one where I could commit to watching it at the given airtime.

claims.claim: MediaProbe generally offers about $5 per hour of watch time, sometimes more.
claims.quote: Generally, media probe offers about $5 per hour of watch time, sometimes a little bit higher, which isn't a bad gig.

claims.claim: The host says the pay will not add up to a full-time income.
claims.quote: If you were gonna be watching anyways, but is never gonna add up to a full-time income.

claims.claim: The host received payment as soon as the following day.
claims.quote: I've gotten paid as soon as the next day, which brings me to drawback number four.

claims.claim: At the time of recording, the host says MediaProbe paid only in gift cards.
claims.quote: At the time of this recording, media probe only pays in gift cards.

claims.claim: The host says there were hundreds of gift cards to choose from.
claims.quote: Now, to their credit, they've got hundreds to choose from, but if you were hoping for a direct cash to your bank, or Venmo or PayPal, you had a luck.

claims.claim: The host's session was denied after he stopped watching before the required time.
claims.quote: It was a World Cup match where I was supposed to leave the post-game show on for like at least 30 minutes, and I probably cut it off after 10 or 15.

claims.claim: The host earned $10 from the MrBeast session and $30 from watching two World Cup games.
claims.quote: In total, I made 10 bucks from MrBeast and 30 bucks from watching a couple World Cup games.

acquisition_channels.details: Panelists apply; the host describes a screening call and session invitations sent to their inbox.

ideas.delivery: MediaProbe mails approved participants a sensor. Participants use the app and phone microphone during assigned shows, attach the electrode readers, and answer questions afterward. MediaProbe sells the resulting audience data and pays participants a share.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 may apply to personal data collected through the sensor and phone microphone. The operator would need a lawful basis and clear privacy information; assess whether special-category biometric rules apply based on the processing purpose.

stated_problem.quote: Now, I actually had one session get denied, 'cause I didn't complete the full watch time.
stated_problem.speaker: Side Hustle Nation host (unnamed)

idea.name: Early-exit session warning
idea.one_liner: Add an in-app confirmation warning before a participant exits a session before completing the required watch time.
idea.offer: A warning that asks users to confirm before leaving a session early.
idea.revenue_model: Not stated; this is a requested feature for an existing app.

key_quotes.quote: A little warning in the app would have been nice, like, hey, you're about to quit your session early, are you sure you wanna do that?

claims.claim: The host was meant to watch at least 30 minutes but stopped after 10 or 15.
claims.quote: It was a World Cup match where I was supposed to leave the post-game show on for like at least 30 minutes, and I probably cut it off after 10 or 15.

ideas.delivery: A confirmation prompt in the MediaProbe app would appear when a participant tries to leave a session before the required watch time.
